text: The lot for the descendants of Joseph ran from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, through the wilderness that climbs from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
From Bethel it went on to Luz and crossed over to the territory of the Archites at Ataroth.
Then it went down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and on to Gezer, and it ended at the Great Sea.

versions.text: Then it went down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and on to Gezer, and it ended at the sea.
versions.explanation: For hearers, "the sea" is unclear; the reference is to the Mediterranean. Either specify it here (as "the Great Sea") or add a footnote at the first occurrence explaining that "the sea" denotes the Mediterranean.

text: So the descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
This was the territory of the Ephraimites, clan by clan: the boundary of their inheritance ran from Ataroth-addar on the east to Upper Beth-horon,
From there the boundary ran westward, with Michmethath on the north, and it turned eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passed by it on the east of Janoah.

versions.text: and from there out to the sea. Michmethath lay to the north, and the boundary turned eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passed by it on the east to Janoah.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מִמִּזְרַח יָנוֹחָה means "on the east of Janoah," describing the location of the boundary relative to Janoah, not motion toward it. "On the east to Janoah" is ambiguous and can be misheard when read aloud.

versions.text: and from there out to the sea. Michmethath lay to the north, and the boundary turned eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passed by it on the east of Janoah.
versions.explanation: הַיָּמָּה here functions directionally ("seaward" = westward) rather than indicating that the border actually reached the Mediterranean; the sea itself is only reached in verse 8 ("ended at the sea"). Rendering it "westward" avoids the impression of two separate arrivals at the sea and keeps the itinerary clear for hearers. Joining the clauses also removes the abrupt full stop mid-itinerary, which reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Then it went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and came out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the boundary ran west to the Kanah Ravine and ended at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim, clan by clan,

versions.text: From Tappuah the boundary ran west to the Wadi Kanah and ended at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim, clan by clan,
versions.explanation: "The Wadi Kanah" mixes an English article with a transliterated Semitic term and reads awkwardly aloud; a plain English rendering such as "the Kanah Ravine" (or "the Kanah Valley") flows better for hearers.

versions.text: From Tappuah the boundary ran west to the Kanah Ravine and ended at the sea.
versions.explanation: The second half of the Hebrew verse — זֹאת נַחֲלַת מַטֵּה בְנֵי־אֶפְרַיִם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם, "This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim according to their clans" — was dropped in an earlier revision. It must be restored; it is also needed as the antecedent for the continuation in verse 9. The improved "Kanah Ravine" wording is retained.

text: together with all the towns and their villages that were set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites.
But they did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. So the Canaanites have lived among the Ephraimites to this day, subjected to forced labor.
